To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
licorice-derived compounds, especially quercetin, are promising candidates as anti-EBV agents and anti-tumor agents against EBVaGC.

quercetin induces more apoptosis in SENU719 cells than isoliuriritigenin, completely eliminates DNMT1 and DMNT3A expressions than isolatequiritigenin, induces signal transductions that stimulate apoptosis more strongly, and reduces EBV latency more effectively than isolatequiritigenein.
quercetin induces apoptosis and inhibits the proliferation of EBVaGC cell line SNU719, and quercetin inhibits EBV infection and reduces the EBV latency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the anti-viral and anti-tumor effects of quercetine against Epstein-Barr virus and EBV associated gastric cancer.
the development of new drugs against EBV infection and EBVaGC.
the antiviral and anticancer effects of the quercetin and the isoliquiritigenen against EBV and the EBVaGC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quercetin has more anti-EBV effects than isoliquiritinigenin.
quercetin is more potent in anti-viral and anti-cancer activity than isoliquiritinigenin.
quercetin induces apoptosis and reduces EBV latency and replication, whereas isoliquirigenin induces apoptosis, but increases EBV latency and EBV progeny.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quercetin is more effective than isoliquiritinigenin in anti-tumor and anti-viral effects against EBVaGC.
quercetin has more antitumor and anti-EBV effects than isoliquiritinigenin.
quercetin is a promising candidate for anti-EBVaGc agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flavonoid quercetin is a potent inhibitor of EBV infection and EBV associated human gastric cancer.
quercetin is an effective antitumor and anti-EBV agent, and quercetin is more effective than isoliquiritinigenin.
the flavonol quercetin is more effective than the chalcone isoliquiritigen in preventing the infection of EBV and the proliferation of EBV-associated human gastric carcinoma cells.
